Playback settings also carry independent device-type zoom defaults and the saved upscaling preference; guide-refresh cadence remains local because LiveTVViewSettingsStore keys are outside the transferable allowlist.

FeatureSyncSetup.summary: Explain reachable receiver/sender setup, local network and scan permissions, code/QR alternatives, conditional verification and provider transfer limits. Same-account rendezvous and scanned QR pin the recipient key; ordinary links do not silently bypass verification.

FeatureWatchlist.summary: The focused Watchlist guide covers saving, removal, navigation, filtering and sorting on Apple TV/iPhone/iPad. Shared UI exposes All/Movies/TV Shows, Clear Filters, Date Added/Release Date/Name and Order. Save dates are distinct from library import; undated entries follow dated entries. Verified accessible library ownership can supply native title/artwork during union or later presentation resolution while preserving the explicit save identity/date; artwork policy still chooses the displayed image. This has a reader-facing explanation, not a new control. The profile-scoped browse model and transfer allowlist preserve browse choices, independently of Home row order. Document explicit saves plus enabled-destination contributions, minus explicit removals. Jellyfin/Emby contribute Favorites; Plex and Silo contribute Watchlists. Disabling a server retracts native contributions without erasing explicit saves. Plex user selection determines native identity; decline excludes that list without disabling browsing/playback, and disabling/re-enabling clears the decline for another choice. Confirmed native-list removals after acknowledged additions can propagate; genuine re-adds can supersede removal. Failed reads/deliveries are not confirmed deletions and are retried. Pending Removing and optimistic local confirmation are not proof that every remote destination accepted the change. Native timestamps, release-date payloads and ownership enrichment support this workflow, not another settings page.

LastFmService.summary: Apple TV music reporting and the connected Use Last.fm pause switch are reachable. Listening-history read support has no production browser entry point, and Last.fm is not a movie/episode history-sync source. Mobile Music does not send its scrobbles.

MALService.summary: Connected-account activation pauses reporting locally without removing Watchlist destinations. Optional 2-way sync can bring watched-only anime history into explicitly selected media shares, not managed servers. Aggregate show episode counts do not identify individual watched episodes. Reviewed bulk import/export views have no production entry point.

MediaDownloads.summary: Explain network/speed/provider limits and completed-copy validation: Finishing or all bytes received is not Downloaded. Selection uses source/item/version identities; episodes can save several copies while movies are single-select, and Ask Each Time cannot bypass batch/multiversion review. Original keeps embedded tracks. New reduced Plex/Emby/Silo copies require all reported audio, validated before completion; formats can change. Emby packages separately prepared compressed audio with converted video and needs temporary storage. Silo rejects an incomplete or changed exact-file audio inventory. Jellyfin reduced copies may keep one track; saved older preparations retain inclusion flags on retry. Jellyfin and Emby without all-audio support require uncapped rendition transfer; new all-audio Emby uses rate-limited/background HTTP. Management is copy-specific; playback tries matching usable copies with the requested version first, even after another server is selected. Background HTTP differs from share work and continued processing remains an OS decision. Profile changes pause transfers; returning resumes under network policy. Movie/episode menus manage a copy; show menus manage a group, and the saved-show Edit/Select All/Remove flow confirms selected episode deletion without touching originals. OfflineMediaProvider reconstructs authorized movies/shows/seasons/episodes from completed physically usable records, artwork, supported local subtitles and local progress. Offline Mode replaces mobile browsing and filters Watchlist without deleting online saves; it is shared on this device. Plex Home's prior-online-sign-in proof is binding-specific and never bypasses a protected PIN or authorizes a new identity. Sidecars share the version/profile folder and removal lifecycle. Supported SRT/VTT/ASS/SSA text, 64 tracks, 16 MiB per file and 64 MiB total are implementation limits; partial warnings keep usable video/good prior sidecars. Subtitle-only updates recheck authorization/network/speed without retransferring video. Explicit-version offline selection never silently substitutes another saved version.

MediaTransportCore.omitReason: Internal file-system capability and bounded-read contracts expose no independent reader setting or procedure. Protocol selection, authentication, scanning and download limits are documented under connections and offline viewing instead.

MediaTransportFTP.summary: Cover FTP and manually addressed implicit FTPS in the share task; composition does not produce explicit AUTH TLS connections. Direct external playback is VLC-only for compatible plain FTP and credential encoding, not FTPS. Other eligible regular files can instead use the separately documented authorized mobile share relay; Apple TV has no such background relay.

MediaTransportHTTP.omitReason: Shared HTTP sessions and trust/range plumbing are not a separately selectable library type in the add-share UI. Document direct-response file-change checks and the credential-isolated HTTPS delivery exception in network-shares#webdav-lists-files-but-will-not-play, not as another source or an internal-settings procedure.

MediaTransportNFS.summary: State the wired NFSv3 requirement and export-based access rules in the network-share procedure, not a separate protocol guide.

MediaTransportWebDAV.summary: A wired share transport, not a media server. Successful listings can lack required playback metadata. Direct range responses need a strong ETag or valid Last-Modified. The authorized locator must retain stable DAV file identity and size, revalidated on opening. For playback only, a supported cross-origin HTTPS delivery response in an isolated anonymous session can omit both validator headers; malformed/weak-only headers do not qualify. Range and size checks still apply, but same-size changes within that delivery stream cannot be detected and persistent byte reuse is disabled. Share credentials are not forwarded to the delivery host. Network shares explains the distinction, administrator checks and stop/rescan/reopen after file replacement. Direct external playback requires an independent compatible HTTP URL with supported anonymous/signed or Basic authorization and system certificate trust; custom links exclude password-bearing URLs. Pinned trust, bearer/custom headers and incompatible password encoding prevent direct handoff. Eligible mobile regular files can use the separate authorized background relay instead.

MetadataKit.summary: Keep provider ordering/cache controls in metadata, lyric availability and LRCLIB title/artist/duration sharing in music, and community skips in playback. The artwork guide explains that interface language requests localized TMDB/TheTVDB posters, not translated library images; provider ranking falls back when language-specific artwork is absent. ArtworkEnvironment carries locale/source policy and ArtworkRouter keys poster caches by the applicable provider language. TVDB preserves regional/script locale variants. The music area traces the device-wide toggle into the lyric resolver's online-query gate. Home explains selecting public Discovery catalogues independently of Seerr requests, with Kids restrictions and no implied playable ownership. This is recommendation discovery, not the FeatureDiscovery module's LAN server search. Marker requests include applicable title/episode metadata and runtime, not video uploads; server markers and third-party coverage remain distinct. Regional release/watch-offer information on external/discovery details is independent of Seerr. Upcoming also consumes episode schedules through SeriesScheduleResolver and regional digital movie-release events through ExternalTitleMetadataResolver; watched/in-progress shows, saved movies and authorized personal requests supply interests. The calendar guide explains missing matching/dates, retained dates during source failure and why dates grant neither playback nor subscription access. TMDB's authorized videos API can supply trailer links after server-owned files and server metadata are considered; it does not verify YouTube availability. Explain the reachable external handoff in library, not a nonexistent streaming-trailer provider or scraping workflow.

ProviderIPTV.summary: Keep playlist/Xtream and EPG setup, scoped guide credentials, local account-file imports, guide-only operation and optional on-demand catalogues in existing source/library tasks. HTTP/proxy/parsing diagnostics do not add a selectable source type. Explicit account setup starts authorized guide preparation beyond the sheet lifetime; stage/current-listing status and Refresh guide recovery differ from channel availability. External-player handoff admits on-demand movies/episodes only when their playable URL needs no extra headers and the request needs no reduced/forced conversion; it excludes live channels and does not add IPTV downloads. Refresh while open updates only saved IPTV guide URLs and due saved lineups; it retains normal on-use/manual refresh paths.

ProviderJellyfin.summary: Keep provider sign-in, library and music behavior in their tasks. The optional Jellyfin-only server-ratings seam reads same-origin authenticated MDBList Ratings CachedByItemId data without fetching upstream services or running plugin refresh/scripts. Detail enrichment prefers valid nonempty results with fallback on absence/failure; Home consumes already-cached results. No new Plozz token or switch is required, and this API must not be inferred for Emby.

ProviderPlex.summary: Plex library, quality, music and guidance remain provider-specific. Extras retain their own identity and do not complete the main title or fan out to trackers/matching copies. Explicitly classified Plex extras receive durable local progress fallback isolated by profile, account and server user, surviving provider refresh on this device. LocalMediaWatchStore keeps at most 2,000 newest records within its payload budget, so older fallback positions can be evicted. A newer usable server history record takes precedence. The library extras section and sync history section explain the reader-visible behavior without promising unlimited retention or cloud transfer of local fallback.

ProviderShare.summary: Network shares covers connection/scanning, Personal Videos and local NFO/artwork association. Keep your place explains durable profile/account-local watched/resume state on this device, separate from iCloud preferences and matching-copy history propagation. LocalMediaWatchStore retains at most 2,000 newest records per profile/source and may retain fewer within its payload budget; eviction can remove old marks/positions. Dismissal from Continue Watching preserves resume; later playback restores eligibility. Imported streaming-service titles use one allowlisted HTTPS title URL in a UTF-8 .strmlnk file up to 8192 bytes; select its source/version and the destination-specific action or Open Link. ExternalMediaLink validates service hosts/title paths. TV requires an installed universal-link app; mobile uses app/browser routing. Opening rechecks authorization and reports Couldn't Open Link rather than starting a stream. Such links create no external-player receipt or automatic returned progress and cannot download; service access/regions remain outside Plozz. Ordinary playable share files separately support compatible direct WebDAV/plain-FTP handoff or a mobile relay. The relay requires a real iOS/iPadOS 26 background grant, a regular immutable file and a noncustom installed player. It excludes playlists, .strm links, ISO and BDMV; returning Plozz to foreground or losing execution/authorization stops the connection. Local metadata precedence and ambiguous-folder rejection are source-verified. Complete decrypted BDMV folders are one title using the index identity and movie-root metadata; disc-playback explains menus/videos, which never gain downloads or external handoff.

ProviderSilo.summary: Silo library channels are reachable on all platforms through shared automatic/custom channel management. Server capability/permission checks require available protocol-3 original-file delivery; eligible single-file versions need reliable runtime/size and are revalidated before playback. Channel transport suppresses ordinary resume writes; default-off completion reporting is separate. Silo still has no native Live TV. Separately, on-demand original/converted streams now support external handoff when account authorization and the playback grant cover the full duration plus the safety margin; incompatible delivery stays in Plozz. New reduced downloads require the complete exact-file audio inventory and reject incomplete/changed prepared tracks; older saved preparations keep their inclusion flags. Encrypted iCloud setup can enroll a distinct device-bound session when protocol-2 session binding is supported and the chosen Silo profile has no PIN. It does not copy rotating device sessions or PIN authorization; nearby transfer still excludes Silo credentials.

SeerService.summary: Profile-bound authenticated Seerr accounts and authorized API-key connections, multi-account request routing, explicit reauthentication and restricted-user/admin handling. User sessions do not transfer; supported profile keys do. Reader procedures live in Media requests.

SimklService.summary: Connected-account activation pauses reporting locally without removing Watchlist destinations. The reachable 2-way sync control can bring supported watched history and compatible resume positions into explicitly selected media shares only. Reviewed bulk import/export views have no production entry point.

TopShelfKit.summary: Document Apple TV placement and loading Home under each system user before that user's current-user extension has saved media. Local visibility/layout/count preferences are shared among Plozz profiles, not an assurance of shared shelf contents across system users. Retain same-copy deduplication, playback versus details actions and current access checks. The carousel buttons have OS-owned captions, not verified app labels. Full-screen metadata uses known source facts, series artwork and spoiler policy, never a guarantee of output or a live server browser. Poster/backdrop composition is infrastructure, not another reader control.

TraktService.summary: Separate Watchlist sync, completed watches and partial pause progress returned by supported external players. Mark as Unwatched does not delete Trakt history. Shared sign-in recovery belongs in trackers; receipt/debug response plumbing needs no separate user procedure. Connected-account activation pauses reporting locally without removing Watchlist destinations. The reachable 2-way sync control can bring supported watched history and compatible resume positions into explicitly selected media shares only. Reviewed bulk import/export views have no production entry point.

WetrakrService.summary: Production-enabled but configuration-gated video tracking and planning-list read/write integration is reachable on both platforms. Cover authorization and connection recovery in trackers and list propagation in library. View on WeTrakr, when present for imported entries, is an external link/TV QR handoff rather than media playback; this self-explanatory link needs no standalone guide. Connected-account activation pauses reporting locally without removing Watchlist destinations. The reachable 2-way sync control can bring supported watched history and compatible resume positions into explicitly selected media shares only. Reviewed bulk import/export views have no production entry point.

ProviderSubsonic.summary: Beta-only Navidrome (Subsonic) provider selection on Apple TV and iPhone/iPad leads to explicit HTTP/HTTPS address, username and Password/API Key sign-in. Music-only browsing includes albums, artists, tracks, playlists and genres, server favorites and duration-qualified listening reports independent of Last.fm. API-key compatibility and username validation are enforced by the provider. No video, downloads, server discovery or alternate-address management is exposed. Source credentials can restore through the shared encrypted cloud credential channel without granting new access.

PublicMetaDBService.summary: Production UI exposes profile-scoped connection via TV browser pairing/manual key or mobile key entry, local playback activation, failure status and optional incoming media-share history. Synced key replacement/disconnect does not revoke the remote key or erase history. Verified movie/episode reporting and watched/resume reads are wired in both shells. Public construction disables accountToolsEnabled: remote list/rating/mapping/history-management/export tools and the PublicMetaDB Watchlist destination are not current reader workflows.

appearance.summary: Keep theme/cards orientation in Appearance, with linked focused artwork and Circadian tasks. The artwork guide follows preset selection and Home, Libraries, Across the app in UI order, explains source tradeoffs and platform-specific rows, and links safe download image recovery. Labels presets replace custom page defaults/row overrides; contextual editors share those preferences. Watch marks, episode counts and progress bars have independent controls without changing history. Spoiler Protection remains in Screens & Navigation > All screens, not Appearance.

language.summary: Use the appearance guide to explain System language selection and distinguish interface language from audio, subtitles, server-supplied metadata and device-region date/number formatting rather than a separate picker guide. The artwork guide explains localized online posters, language-neutral/provider fallback and unchanged library images; valid saved download images are not replaced by a language change. System-drawn player controls and permission prompts keep the device language.

libraries.summary: Explain shared sign-ins versus profile-selected accounts/server users and library discovery switches. Choose a server user covers TV Watching as, mobile picker/Plex identity rows, PIN checks and Add Another User/Add Another Plex Account. Added logins are shared by profiles on this device; no server user is created. Disabled libraries hide browsing/discovery, not account-wide Continue Watching/Next Up, and are not permission or maturity filters. Showing a navigation shortcut is a separate task: mobile libraries start hidden, and All Libraries combines at least two enabled browsable non-music libraries on all three platforms. Keep music eligibility in its platform-specific task.

liveTV.summary: The channel guide's Choose where Live TV opens section explains Categories versus Guide, Channel order and Guide preferences > Recently watched, with profile/device-local persistence. Keep previews, favorites/hidden channels, search and mobile network policy in existing Live TV guides rather than separate toggle pages. Settings orders Guide & browsing before Channel names, then mobile Playback. Clean channel names defaults on and tidies only IPTV display labels; manual names win, Preview uses loaded samples and Example supplies a fallback without changing guide matching, favorites or source data. Distinguish the Wi-Fi-only setting's detected-transition limit from Low Data Mode's independent pause, including on Wi-Fi. Explain local whole-source Kids approval and source-configuration sync separately. Shared TV Sources/Add TV Source labels differ from household Sources. Guide preparation and Refresh guide need recovery instructions, not one page per progress stage. Guide preferences ends with Refresh while open, default Every 12 hours. It controls foreground updates of already-saved IPTV account lineups/guides, stays profile/device-local and preserves on-use updates when Off.

playback.summary: Cover version mode/series memory, autoplay/skips, quality, audio, background listening, orientation/gestures and history with platform/provider gates. Ask to resume or start over is independent of resume rewind/version selection. Player tabs opens from the Player section on both platforms, ordering default-on Chapters, Cast, Episodes, Playlist and Continue Watching; content still gates cards and Info cannot be hidden. Audio includes default-on Identify songs using Shazam and decoded playback audio, not the microphone. Every Info match card opens service choices; Apple Music alone needs a supplied song URL. Internet, active supported playback and route checks apply; Offline Mode prevents recognition. Skip settings distinguish enablement, categories, button/delay and per-marker Off; community requests are separate. Series audio memory requires its switch and stores language, not commentary/mix; manually selected movie audio language is remembered without that switch. Per-profile movie/series zoom memory is also independent of the track-memory switches. Default-on Prefer lossless audio is shared on this device, not synced/transferred; disabling requests compressed surround-compatible AetherEngine output for newly loaded video/live streams, not a guaranteed hardware format or native/external setting. Video buffer and separate Live TV buffer affect new loads, not downloads. Version selection offers ask, automatic and server order; automatic uses remembered type or device ranking, while server order ignores memory. Its information action explains ranking without another mode. Advanced > External player is device-wide; the reference explains compatible original/converted streams, expanded provider/share routes, actual mobile background-grant requirements, token/password sharing, fallback and authorized progress returns. Discs precedes Advanced; the profile defaults to Play video, with Open disc menu for attemptable share folders and one-time held-play alternatives. HDMV-only compatibility and suppressed menu/video-list history remain in the disc guide. Default player zoom adds independent phone/tablet/television profile defaults, initially Normal, with Custom revealing Zoom. Video upscaling stores Off/Automatic/Standard/Animation, initially Automatic, for new playback; actual SDR enhancement remains hardware/display/engine constrained, and the player session override does not rewrite it.

screensNavigation.summary: Screens & Navigation uses Home, Libraries and Movie & show details. Home orders Hero, Apple TV-only Row style, Card labels, Rows and Filtering. Hero uses On/Off on Apple TV and Show hero on mobile; Classic/Showcase row style is independent of hero visibility. Preserve presets, default-on Next Up merging and saved-row recovery. Rows > Add row > Custom row opens Content, Name, Sort, Filter, Layout, conditional Logo and preview. Content can combine multiple collections, video playlists, accessible enabled video libraries, Home feeds and recommendations. These saved row queries differ from temporary larger-grid changes; provider/account/user identity and failure recovery remain explicit. Recently Added hides completed titles only when enabled; Hero & discovery hides watched suggestions by default. These independent filters change suggestions, not history/access/Continue Watching. App navigation owns Pinned Sidebar/Sidebar/Top Bar, delayed style application, library shortcuts, explicit Show and Settings recovery; layout/shortcuts stay local. Libraries edits supported profile tabs, Recommended rows and collection covers, not Home/shortcuts. Collection-only directories omit Recommended editing; library/Recommended/Home cover controls are independent and do not style member titles. Logo/Text sizing and contextual labels belong with appearance. All screens owns spoilers/classification display, not scores/restrictions. Movie & show details > Trailers & music opens the shared page: Trailers selects sources, Home contains Home autoplay and conditional Start muted, then Details contains Detail background and conditional Start muted or Theme music volume. Detail background offers mutually exclusive Trailer/Theme music/Off on all platforms, with Trailer dependent on allowed server trailers; audio explains volume, preview/generated fallback and mobile session mute. DetailNavigationTransition is internal animation plumbing, not a user-facing settings workflow; the retired transition key in ProfileSettingsSnapshot does not establish an available control.

subtitles.summary: Combine language codes/device fallback, per-content policies, SDH/search, remembered series choices and text/image styling limits rather than separate pages per preference. Explain Prefer SDH fallback versus strict Only SDH selection and matching device caption appearance with replacement confirmation. Appearance edits leave matching; changing only Auto-Move Away from Controls or Override ASS/SSA styling preserves it. Keep captions near the picture explains default-on control avoidance and the overlap tradeoff. Use your style instead of file formatting explains the three source-formatting toggles, the default-off ASS/SSA override in Settings-only non-Live-TV styling, loss of authored signs/karaoke and explicit restoration. Reset to App Default preserves that override. Change appearance explains Apple TV's full-screen preview and focused sample options versus mobile Preview options; the sample is not the reader's video.

trackers.summary: Guide connection and recovery, per-service pause without disconnect, PublicMetaDB TV pairing/mobile key entry, and optional experimental existing/new tracker history into selected media shares. Keep Last.fm Apple TV-only, WeTrakr configuration-gated, managed-server history outbound-only and iCloud separate. Record unwired account-management/import/export tools as omissions, not reader procedures.

downloads.summary: Mobile-only, feature-gated Downloads category: Offline Mode, network, speed, background, quality and storage choices are explained with download completion and authorization limits. The Settings shortcut is hidden in Kids profiles; Downloads > Download Settings remains an alternative entry.

seerr.summary: Seerr belongs to the active Plozz profile and is hidden in Kids settings. Shared account setup/management supports authenticated users, multiple connections and restricted API-key mappings; Kids setup remains available in the optional profile flow.

Sources/AppShelliOS/PlozziOSProfileAvata.omitReason: The iPhone/iPad profile-picker parent uses this noninteractive avatar/name transition after selection, with a host supplied by RootView. It adds no screen, named control or authorization decision. The snapshot is hidden from accessibility, while the parent supplies the selected profile's accessible name and Loading status. Reduce Motion skips the flight; window resizing recenters it. Profile checks, cancellation, management controls and Offline Mode remain inventoried on PlozziOSProfilePickerView, not on this rendering helper.

Sources/CoreUI/PlozzPlaceholderRail.swif.omitReason: The generic loading-rail helper declares no controls or reader destination. No production source instantiates PlozzPlaceholderRail in this snapshot; its example call is a comment, not an entry point. Existing Home, Discover and detail rails retain their own loading presentations and parent-screen controls.

Sources/CoreUI/PlozzReservedPlaceholder..omitReason: Loading-space reservation and readiness/appearance fades support the mobile detail and profile-picker parents. They add no named control, setting or destination; the parents inventory playable cards, selection and recovery actions. Reduce Motion disables their entrance animation without changing those actions.

Sources/CoreUI/FeaturedCardControl.swift.omitReason: Featured cards are selected through FeaturedMediaRow on the TV/mobile Home parents, whose records inventory their capability-dependent context actions. Titles are dynamic media names. The custom-row editor uses the same artwork with no selection handler and clears navigation/context-action environments in HomeRowPreviewView; it is a visual preview, not another playback destination.

Sources/CoreUI/FeaturedMediaRowPresentat.omitReason: Shared featured-row chrome is reached through FeaturedMediaRow on both Home parents and through HomeRowPreviewView in the custom editor. Production Home callers enable usesRowBrowsing, so mobile uses a dynamic BrowseRowHeading and TV a trailing MediaRowBrowseCard; their controls are inventoried on the parents. The component's legacy See all fallback is therefore not a separate reachable control. Custom-row empty/failure states route through Home section status, and the editor passes loaded items only; neither needs a new empty-collection workflow from this helper's generic caption. The editor clears editing/routing and its preview actions are no-ops.

Sources/CoreUI/HomeContentQueryControls..omitReason: The expanded Home-row browser and custom-row editor both construct these options and inventory them on their parent records. Sort By starts with Source order; selecting a field reveals Order. Media precedes Watch status; Clear Filters appears only with an active filter. The browser's choices are temporary, whereas the editor saves them with its row.

Sources/CoreUI/HomeRowPreviewView.swift.omitReason: CollectionSectionSettingsView owns this custom-row preview below its Content, Name, Sort, Filter and Layout choices. It reproduces poster, landscape or featured rows with profile artwork, captions and spoiler policy. Selection/routing/context actions are cleared and preview browse callbacks are no-ops; it cannot start a video or edit a second row. Parent controls and preview failure recovery are inventoried on that editor.

Sources/CoreUI/OpaqueNavigationChrome.sw.omitReason: The mobile root supplies destination labels and selection to PlozzOpaqueTabBar; its parent inventories those destinations. On iOS/iPadOS 26+, app-requested reduced transparency with system Reduce Transparency off can replace bottom tabs with this horizontally scrolling strip when neither a vertical toolbar nor sidebar is active. The navigation-controller bridge restyles existing buttons without changing captions or adding a settings destination. System reduced transparency retains native tabs.

Sources/FeatureSettings/HomeContentPicke.navigation: Open Settings > Screens & Navigation > Home > Rows > Add row > Custom row > Content, or Content in an existing custom row.
Sources/FeatureSettings/HomeContentPicke.experience: Select several accessible Home feeds, whole libraries, recommendations, collections or video playlists for one custom Home row. Review Selected, undo selections, then use Done to return to the row editor without changing server-side lists.
Sources/FeatureSettings/HomeContentPicke.conditions: TV puts Done in its page header; mobile puts Done in the confirmation toolbar. When selections exist, Selected and removable dynamic source names precede Collections and Playlists, then the Home feeds Continue Watching, Watchlist and Recently Added, each enabled video library and its feeds, then any server-wide Recommended feeds. Libraries exclude music and retired collection shortcuts and require current account inclusion and library visibility. Collection/playlist destinations are capability-gated and preserve the selected server user. New rows allow clearing all choices; existing rows prevent removing the last source. Unavailable saved choices remain visible with Unavailable source; they do not grant access or silently bind to a different server user. Partial source discovery shows Some sources couldn't be loaded. and Retry. Dynamic library, collection, playlist and recommendation names are content, not constant control captions.

Sources/AppShell/PlaybackPresentationHos.omitReason: The Apple TV MainTabViewSupport playback host serializes the player cover and shared resume prompt. It has no labels or separate destination; Resume, Start Over and Cancel remain inventoried on PlaybackResumePrompt, and the video controls on PlayerView.

Sources/CoreUI/DiscPlaybackAction.swift.navigation: Set the default in Settings > Playback > Discs > Disc playback; from eligible title/card actions choose its alternative disc action or Play in.
Sources/CoreUI/DiscPlaybackAction.swift.experience: Choose the alternative Open disc menu or Play video action for a supported disc, or hand an eligible file to a listed installed player. The unavailable-disc reason remains visible when an alternative cannot run.
Sources/CoreUI/DiscPlaybackAction.swift.conditions: Actions require disc-menu availability or nonempty external-player choices. The saved default determines which disc action is the alternative. Play in requires an authorized on-demand movie, episode or video and an eligible provider; external links and disc folders are excluded. It lists installed supported alternatives in platform order, omitting the current default. Plozz can appear when another app is the default; Native Player is Apple TV-only. Custom templates are not offered here. Provider, file and platform capabilities still apply; an installed app does not guarantee a compatible handoff. The same DiscPlayback enum titles also populate the default-setting selector in the two settings shells; those are defaults, while the title action is a one-time alternative.

Sources/FeatureProfiles/ProfileChip.swif.omitReason: The chip displays the dynamic active profile name and avatar, not a switcher or button. Libraries and profile-setup parents use the ProfileLibrariesScope Saved for heading; ProfileSeerrSetupView uses Request as. Those headings are inventoried on their parents rather than inventing a constant profile-name control.

Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlayerDiscContro.omitReason: PlayerControls on Apple TV and PlozziOSPlayerControlsOverlay on iPhone/iPad host the optical-disc button and inventory its Disc menu/Disc videos labels and contextual actions. It appears only for active disc-menu playback or a network-disc source. Menu playback opens the menu; direct playback opens the video list. A held button can offer Play video and, during menu playback, Try another region.

Sources/FeaturePlayback/DiscMenuPlayerCo.navigation: Open a network-share BDMV title's details, choose Open disc menu from its play-button context menu or set Settings > Playback > Discs > Disc playback to Open disc menu. On Apple TV press Back for Plozz's Disc menu dialog; on mobile use its optical-disc actions menu.
Sources/FeaturePlayback/DiscMenuPlayerCo.experience: Navigate the disc's menu with remote directions and center on Apple TV, or tap its artwork/use direction and Select buttons on mobile. After explicit IPTV setup/refresh, a shared guide notice can remain across navigation while the account is authorized. It is hidden behind another transient message. Dismiss hides only the notice; terminal notices also auto-dismiss after five seconds. Percentages describe the current stage, not total work. Profile/account authorization changes cancel and remove scoped work; this does not promise OS background execution. New installations show the shared iCloud consent/restoration flow before normal setup. Both shells can restore supported server/share credentials through encrypted iCloud records, while Silo creates a separately authorized device session only when server capability and PIN-free profile checks succeed. Navigation suppresses Home/Search without relevant content and Watchlist without saved items. Music-only Subsonic connections can land on Music; live-only sources prefer Live TV. Unreachable established media servers retain remembered library navigation rather than treating failure as authoritative emptiness. Existing-sign-in publication permission requires startupPresentationReady, an authorized profile, no active or queued root presentation, Settings closed and no parental-management PIN gate. The service also requires enabled sync, a verified iCloud identity and unchanged eligible sign-ins without a current owner or declined decision.

SubtitleOverlayView uses measured control frames only while avoidance is enabled. SubtitleStyleSettingsView passes showsASSOverride only for the ordinary video Settings editor; the in-player context and separate Live TV Settings style leave it false. Actual primary/secondary text styling and timing remain track/path-dependent.

Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlaybackDiagnost.navigation: Enable Playback Diagnostics Overlay in Help & Diagnostics, then play media.
Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlaybackDiagnost.experience: Read transfer rate, buffers, seekable range and available route/engine telemetry.
Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlaybackDiagnost.conditions: Device-local diagnostic visibility. Mobile lays out Source, Video, Audio, optional Original File, Subtitles, optional Live, Playback, optional Engine and System sections; Apple TV groups them into three columns. Missing measurements omit their rows. Transcoding distinguishes current stream facts from the original file. Plozzigen uses AVPlayer time/window labels; native uses Position/Seekable. Live fields need live-stream telemetry; cache fields need session-cache measurements. Engine statistics supply Decoder, Bridge bitrate and Audio delivery when available. TV combines recent/average bitrate and delivery rate/bytes when both measurements exist; other layouts use separate rows. Local delivery/transferred describes the app's delivery to AVPlayer rather than the source network. Engine appears only with source-byte or restart statistics; its mux and bridge values are internal transfer measurements, not output lip sync or physical speaker facts. Resident memory is distinct from the app's footprint. Encoded bitrate, network throughput, cache capacity and physical audio output are different measurements.

Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlaybackOptionsP.navigation: On Apple TV, move up from the timeline and select the current-rate Playback Speed button for Speed, or More for Zoom Mode, Upscaling and Version.

Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlaybackOptionsP.conditions: Apple TV card UI. Speed is a separate speedOnly pane requiring playbackSpeed; it is not inside More. More places caller-supplied rows first, then Zoom Mode, Upscaling and Version when eligible. Each needs its engine/content capability; Upscaling additionally needs a ready, reloadable, seekable on-demand stream. Quality conversion uses separate mobile surfaces. Auto-crop needs active-picture support, wired in both production movie factories, and local ready visible playback; external playback/PiP stops sampling. Invalid detection fits normally; proportional cropping need not fill all edges. Movie/episode framing uses the platform default, initially Normal, unless a profile-owned movie/series override exists; strong matches across servers can reuse it independently of track memory. Extras/trailers and unidentified disc timelines do not use title memory; new live channels use the default without per-channel memory. TV uses More > Zoom Mode; mobile uses Zoom in Playback options/Playback settings. Upscaling's Off/Automatic/Standard/Animation choices affect only the current session, show Applying… during a position-preserving reload and report failure without changing the saved default. Live TV, disc menus, separate-audio and custom-reader share streams omit that session switch. Version opens a nested picker only for multiple versions.

With the surface focused and no active scrub, a light stationary touch reveals a hidden timeline; the next shows current/estimated finish times and the next hides controls. A center click instead pauses/plays or commits a seek. The estimate needs valid duration/speed, and the next reveal resets to elapsed/remaining time. Sources/FeaturePlayback/PlayerControls.s.conditions: Apple TV. Tracks, chapters, sequence, versions and playback engine capabilities gate cards; missing data is not supplied by an unrelated provider. Sources/FeatureSettings/PublicMetaDBAcco.omitReason: This mixed helper file is not an account-tools destination. PublicMetaDBSettingsContent constructs its reachable PublicMetaDBTrackingRows: activation, conditional reporting-failure text, then enabled share-sync rows, all audited in those parents. TrackerHistoryImportFailure also reuses PublicMetaDBFailureMessage for reachable sync errors. The paged arbitrary-record/catalogue helpers are used only by deferred account tools: production PublicMetaDBService disables accountToolsEnabled and supplies no management entry point.

Sources/FeatureSettings/PublicMetaDBPlay.omitReason: Read-only failure text is embedded after the activation switch by PublicMetaDBTrackingRows on the connected account page. The text is not a retry button or a separate screen.

Do not document Compare again, conflict overrides or Apply selected changes as current account actions.

Sources/FeatureSettings/PublicMetaDBSett.navigation: Open Settings > Trackers > PublicMetaDB. The connected page places Use PublicMetaDB, any reporting issue and eligible Watch history controls above Account. Connect PublicMetaDB starts browser pairing on Apple TV or secure key entry on iPhone/iPad.
Sources/FeatureSettings/PublicMetaDBSett.experience: Connect the chosen profile to PublicMetaDB, verify Connected, pause playback reporting, recover a saved key, or explicitly replace/disconnect it. Apple TV pairing shows a QR/website and dynamic pairing code, with manual key entry as an alternative. Read failures without assuming a report succeeded or repeating an uncertain watch.
Sources/FeatureSettings/PublicMetaDBSett.conditions: Both production shells provide the tracking service and fenced media-share history session. The key field is secure; values/codes are private dynamic data. Enter API key manually is Apple TV-only; mobile starts with API key and Connect. Replace API key requires confirmation, replaces this profile's key on synced devices and does not revoke the old key remotely. Disconnect also requires confirmation, removes the synced key and preserves history. Connected tracking requires verified title/episode identity and local playback activation; paused status refresh does not re-enable consent. Sync choices are local and optional. Account-tools clients remain gated off: no list/rating/history-management or community-contribution destinations are reachable.

Sources/FeatureSettings/TrackerHistorySy.navigation: Settings > Trackers > a connected enabled video/anime tracker or PublicMetaDB > Watch history. 2-way sync is inline. Enabling with multiple shares opens Libraries to sync; one share starts without a chooser. Libraries expands the current selection after enabling.
Sources/FeatureSettings/TrackerHistorySy.experience: Explicitly bring existing and new compatible tracker watched/resume history back to selected network shares in this profile. Choose shares, start, read progress and expand the last-sync summary for per-library outcomes. Use Sync now for later or interrupted checks, or stop without undoing previously applied history.
Sources/FeatureSettings/TrackerHistorySy.conditions: Experimental. Available only for enabled trackers with eligible media-share accounts and supported history categories, or an enabled previous permission needing removal. The production runtime grants only mediaShare scope; Plex/Emby/Silo/Jellyfin are never incoming targets. Shares are named dynamically and disambiguated by server user; transport marks do not change destination scope. TV puts Start sync/Cancel above the chooser and mobile uses toolbar actions. At least one share must be selected; deselecting the last active share disables sync. Watched and compatible resumes are selected from supported categories; AniList/MyAnimeList expose watched only and aggregate counts do not identify episodes. Existing history is included at initial enrollment. Index/history must be complete; conflicts, missing/ambiguous matches, incompatible runtime and destructive clearing are not automatically overwritten. Playing titles defer, unconfirmed deliveries are held rather than blindly repeated, and rate-limit/read/save failures stay visible. Activation changes fence current work; a still-matching saved permission can resume when reporting is re-enabled. Profile/account/source changes can make the saved permission obsolete. Foreground checks require the authorized active profile; mobile excludes Offline Mode. No entitlement or background mode promises a background history import.
